Back in the bad old days, cruise control didn't check the engine speed against the car's speed and therefore had no way of knowing if the car had lost traction or not. Losing traction with the old cruise control turned on was not a good thing; unless you turned it off, almost immediately, the car would quickly skid out of control.

I was a witness to one such incident on a highway at about 120 km/h in rainy weather conditions. The car flipped side over side and end over end and landed on the roof, with three of us in the car. I was in the back seat and, back in the bad old days, none of the seat belts in the back were equipped with shoulder belts. I ended up with about 35 stitches for my part; mostly in my face and arm.

I know that cruise control is a bit smarter now, but I am still hesitant to use it in inclement weather; if I do use it in bad weather, I am always poised to shut it off in an instant, even though I know that there is programming to do it, probably before I'd notice that there is a loss of traction. Sensors and programs can and do fail, So anybody that asks me, I recommend not using cruise when road conditions are questionable.
